svg.title: Bound the entire handoff, not only published queue items
svg.desc: Independent teaching fixtures • no queue implementation or measured performance
svg.text: Bound the entire handoff, not only published queue items
Independent teaching fixtures • no queue implementation or measured performance
Acceptance transfers responsibility
Accepted → queue owns this logical item
Full / Closed → producer retains responsibility
Dequeue → consumer owns the next decision
Reserve item count and bytes together
Published Q + reserved R ≤ item bound
Queued bytes + reserved bytes ≤ byte bound
Failed publication rolls back credit once
Independent byte fixture: 3 items / 10 bytes
A6 accepted; B5 rejects for bytes
C4 accepted: 2 items / 10 bytes
Dequeue A; accept B: 2 items / 9 bytes
Downstream work needs its own bound
Queue limit 2 + in-flight limit 3 = 5
Only if no other retained population exists
Future KV and output bounds remain separate
An unbounded caller backlog can defeat a bounded queue; measure where pressure moves.
FIFO describes the agreed acceptance order, not external arrival or completion order.
